# Serialise audits at the shared local resource, not per host or per repo

## Problem statement

Audit runs are serialised **per host** (and, on the fallback path, per worklog/repo), but the resource they actually contend for is the **single local `llama-server` GPU** that every host and project shares. With two agent hosts and four projects, the per-host guards permit N concurrent audits against one GPU: on 2026-11-03 08:30–09:10 five audits plus a plan run overlapped and drew 592,452 prompt tokens / 4,345 decoded tokens across 30 streams in 40 minutes — almost pure prefill on one GPU. Each host enforces "one audit per host", so one GPU sees two audits; and the audit skill's per-project batch queue does not serialise across projects either.

## Users

- **Operator running multiple projects on two hosts** — wants at most one audit-tier session on the local GPU at a time, regardless of which project or host launched it.
- **herdr downtime dispatcher** — needs an authoritative, lease-derived admission signal so it never dispatches an audit the proxy will refuse at first byte.
- **Audit skill batch drain** — needs a cross-project queue so a batch item from repo A and one from repo B serialise, with reporting that shows which projects contributed.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, I want at most one audit-tier session running against the local `llama-server` across all my hosts and projects, **so that** audits stop thrashing the single GPU.
- As the herdr downtime dispatcher, I want the capacity decision to consume the same availability signal the proxy enforces, **so that** a dispatched audit is never refused at admission.
- As an operator, I want the audit-batch drain to report `items_included` across projects, **so that** I can verify cross-project serialisation is actually happening.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Proxy-side audit admission token.** A proxy-side audit admission token (or an equivalent shared-resource gate) exists such that at most one audit-tier session holds it across all client hosts; a second audit waits rather than competing. The token is identified and released for the whole audit lifetime, with a TTL/staleness backstop.
- **AC2 — Cross-project audit-batch queue.** An audit dispatched for repo A and one for repo B are serialised by the same queue, and the batch drain reports `items_included` across projects (each item drains against its own worklog root).
- **AC3 — Dispatcher uses lease-derived availability.** The dispatcher's capacity decision uses the lease-derived availability signal (see the sibling lease-occupancy item LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5), not raw version counts, and the mismatch between dispatcher admission and proxy refusal is impossible.
- **AC4 — Tested and documented.** Two concurrent audit dispatches from two different hosts (simulated distinct client identities) result in one running and one waiting, with a log line per decision. Documentation is updated (gate table, machine-dir files, log vocabulary, operator runbook).
- **AC5 — ContextHub child item.** A ContextHub child item records the single-machine limitation of `~/.herdr/downtime` and the chosen cross-machine mechanism.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation.** Unit and integration tests cover the gate (single holder, waiting second, clean release, stale-lease expiry, fail-safe on proxy error) and the cross-project queue routing; changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC7 — Docs.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC8 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Out of scope

- Changing slot count, context size, or the prefill-serialisation cap (`local_max_concurrent_prefills`).
- Changing the residency rules or the prefix-warmth pricing themselves (owned by LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI and its sibling).
- A general-purpose distributed lock service; the gate must reuse the proxy's existing admission surface.
- The `dev`→`main` release (ship skill).
- Any broader multi-machine herdr leader election beyond the audit-admission mechanism.

## Constraints

- **Repository span: the software-factory control infrastructure, not the audited repos.** The item is *tracked in the `llm` worklog*, and the code that implements the factory's control plane currently lives in three repositories: `llm` (proxy admission), `SorraAgents` (audit skill client + shared queue — `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit` resolves to `SorraAgents/skill/audit`), and `ContextHub` (herdr dispatcher). **"Three" matters only as "the control-infrastructure repos", not as a count**: the factory audits many other repositories (e.g. fire audits on unrelated projects), but those are *targets* of the factory, not part of its control software. The scope boundary is therefore "the repos that implement audit admission, dispatch and the shared queue", and the audited repos are unaffected. Precedent for cross-repo tracking in this worklog: LP-0MSQ79OBO0019CNP ("tests land in `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py`; work item tracked in llm worklog").
- The proxy is the only component both agent hosts already talk to, so a proxy-side gate is the natural shared resource.
- The gate must be **fail-safe**: a proxy error must not block every audit indefinitely (bounded wait, then a documented fallback).
- Existing single-host behaviour must be preserved: one audit per host still holds; the new gate narrows to one audit across hosts.
- The existing host-wide dispatch-budget ledger (`~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.json`, `maxAudit`) is single-machine only and is authored by each ContextHub host; the cross-machine mechanism must be additive and documented.
- **Budget ownership moves to the proxy.** `budget.json` is currently read per ContextHub host, and ContextHub may run on multiple servers; the proxy is the one place that can hold one authoritative audit budget and the live audit leases. The proxy must therefore own the audit cap and expose availability, and ContextHub must query it rather than assert its own cap (producer direction, 2026-11-09).
- Commit to `dev` only; no direct `main` pushes.

## Existing state

- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/index.ts` `getActiveAudit` already consults the machine-scoped dispatch-budget ledger (`host-dispatch-budget.ts`, kind `audit`, cap `maxAudit`, 2 h staleness) and falls back to the per-worklog dispatch-log check. The `active-audit` marker file is retired (read-compat only).
- `machine-coordination.ts` resolves `~/.herdr/downtime` and documents "single-machine v1 only; multi-machine (flock/NFS) is out of scope". `budget.json` (`maxAudit`) is read per host, so two ContextHub instances on different servers can each believe they are under cap.
- `llm/proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` already issues TTL-bound, single-use local-admission tickets via `POST /llama/local/reserve`, priced by `prefill_eta.evaluate_admission`.
- The audit skill's `audit_runner.py` uses a host-wide `PriorityQueue` at `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-semaphores/audit` (admission tickets) and `.../audit-batch` (batch items). The queue path is host-wide, but entries carry no project identity, so a drain from repo A can dequeue an item meant for repo B.
- The proxy sees `client_ip` and the `X-Session-Id` header (audit sessions are named `audit-<issue>-<context>-<uuid8>`), so it can distinguish hosts and audit-tier sessions.

## Desired change

1. Add a **proxy-side cross-host audit admission gate**: a long-TTL, audit-tier lease (or equivalent shared-resource gate) that admits at most one audit across all client hosts and makes a second wait. Release on audit completion, with a staleness/expiry backstop.
2. Make the **audit-batch queue project-aware**: entries carry their worklog root (or a stable project identity), so a cross-project drain routes each item to its own worklog and reports `items_included` across projects.
3. Make the **herdr dispatcher's capacity decision** consume the same lease-derived availability signal, and record the cross-machine mechanism in a ContextHub child item.
4. **Move audit-budget ownership to the proxy** (producer direction, 2026-11-09): the proxy owns the audit cap and the live lease registry and exposes availability; ContextHub queries it instead of asserting a per-host `budget.json` cap. This makes the dispatcher admission and proxy refusal agree by construction (AC3) even when ContextHub runs on several servers.

## Candidate mechanisms (for AC1)

| Option | Where | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Extend `POST /llama/local/reserve` with a long-TTL audit-tier lease | `llm` proxy | Single gate at the GPU host; reuses the existing ticket/ETA machinery; needs a client-side holder + renewal |
| (b) New `/llama/local/audit/lease` endpoint | `llm` proxy | Cleaner separation from per-request reservations; more surface |
| (c) Shared file/lock on the proxy host (flock/NFS) consumed by dispatchers | ContextHub | Works without a proxy API change; but `~/.herdr/downtime` is local to each host, so this needs a shared filesystem both hosts mount |

**Recommended: (a)** — the proxy already owns admission tickets, and it is the one component both hosts talk to. The producer direction (2026-11-09) strengthens this: the proxy should **own the audit budget** (`audit_admission.max_audits`, default 1) and the live lease registry, with ContextHub querying the proxy's availability rather than reading a per-host `budget.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — extend the ticket model with an audit-tier lease (long TTL, renewal, release), or add a sibling module.
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — new lease endpoint and status surface.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — audit-tier denial/queueing and the audit lease check in the local dispatch path.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — document the audit admission gate, release points and failure modes.
- `SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — acquire/renew/release the audit lease around a run; make batch-queue entries project-aware and report `items_included` across projects.
- `SorraAgents/skill/shared/queue.py` — optional: carry a project/worklog root in `QueueEntry`.
- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` / `downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` use the lease-derived signal.
- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` / `machine-coordination.ts` — cross-machine mechanism and the single-machine limitation note.
- `ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` queries the proxy's audit availability instead of `budget.json` for the audit tier (follow-up item created in the ContextHub worklog).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope creep (3 physical repos).** The audit skill lives in `SorraAgents`, not this repo. Assumption: AC2 lands as a `SorraAgents` change tracked by this item (precedent LP-0MSQ79OBO0019CNP), or a linked child item; this item stays the proxy-side admission spine.
- **Gate deadlock.** A crashed audit that never releases the lease would block all audits. Mitigation: TTL + staleness window + a documented manual release command.
- **Distinguishing audit vs non-audit sessions.** Assumption: audit-tier is identified by the `audit-` `X-Session-Id` prefix; a non-audit session with that prefix would be misclassified, so the gate must log the identity it used.
- **Cross-host clock trust.** TTL/staleness comparisons use the proxy's clock, not each host's, so a skewed host cannot hold a stale lease.
- **Behaviour change risk.** Narrowing from one-audit-per-host to one-audit-globally reduces audit throughput; the operator should confirm the intended cap (default 1).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Extra opportunities discovered during implementation are recorded as linked work items, not absorbed into this item.

## Related work

- **LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5** — Local dispatch lease occupancy must match llama and be diagnosable on denial (completed). The "sibling lease-occupancy item" referenced by AC3; establishes the lease-derived availability source.
- **LP-0MW0VH2LB008JSKQ** — Routing concurrency gate counts the requesting session's own idle lease, pushing returning sessions remote (completed). The lease-gate/routing-gate disagreement this item must not reintroduce.
- **LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI** — Assign the local slot before the admission verdict so prefix residency is measured, not predicted (in progress). Slot-candidate sequencing the audit lease must coexist with.
- **WL-0MVXY0XPF006YUHA** (ContextHub) — F2: Audit tier 1→N generalisation and active-audit unification (completed). Retired the `active-audit` marker in favour of the dispatch-budget ledger.
- **WL-0MVXY0WQF0069YDJ**, **WL-0MVXY0ZYW009NEJD**, **WL-0MVXY10QH0020V7S** (ContextHub) — F1 dispatch-budget ledger, F5 budget observability, F6 docs. Precedents for the ledger + docs pattern.
- **WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB** (ContextHub) — Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type (open).
- **LP-0MSQ79OBO0019CNP** — Precedent for cross-repo audit-skill work tracked in the llm worklog.
- **LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK** — Proxy owns the audit admission budget and exposes availability (child of this item, created 2026-11-09 per producer direction).
- **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS** (ContextHub worklog) — Herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget (discovered-from this item; blocked by LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MSQ7C9TM007L24I** – Docs: update SKILL.md monitored-run + audit-skill-reference (completed)
- **LP-0MVZA6FV20077E6I** – Refactor: Modernization in /home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/worktrees/wl-LP-0MVZ810NG008A3EW-proxy-killed-by-global-oom-gpu-backed-am/proxy/proxy/host_pressure.py (open)
- **LP-0MQL8CNB5005AVF7** – Host ROCm Upgrade: APT repo + driver upgrade (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `proxy/README.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+118 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which repository owns the audit-skill side of AC2?** — Answer (research, self-answered): `SorraAgents/skill/audit`; the installed `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit` is the same inode as `SorraAgents/skill/audit`. Precedent LP-0MSQ79OBO0019CNP tracks audit-skill changes in the llm worklog. Evidence: `readlink -f ~/.pi/agent/skills/audit` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/audit`.
- **Q: Which cross-host mechanism should AC1 use?** — Answer (research + recommendation, advisory only): candidate (a) extend `POST /llama/local/reserve` with an audit-tier lease. The work item explicitly allows "or an equivalent shared-resource gate", so the final choice belongs to the implement stage.
- **Q: Is the audit-tier cap exactly 1 across all hosts, or configurable?** — Answer (from the work item): AC1 says "at most one audit-tier session holds it across all client hosts", so the default cap is 1. Recommended: make it configurable via the same `budget.json`/env mechanism as `maxAudit`, defaulting to 1 so behaviour is unchanged at the cap.
- **Q: Should AC2's cross-project batch drain run from any project, or a designated coordinator?** — Answer (from the work item): AC2 says "an audit dispatched for repo A and one for repo B are serialised by the same queue", so any project may drain; each item must route to its own worklog root.
- **Q: Does it matter that the factory audits other repos that are not part of the factory control software?** — Answer (producer, 2026-11-09): the three repos are the *control infrastructure* (the software factory's control plane); the repos the factory audits (e.g. fire audits) are targets and are unaffected. "Three" describes the control-infrastructure set, not the number of repos in existence. Source: producer reply; recorded in the Constraints section.
- **Q: Should the proxy own the audit budget and ContextHub query it?** — Answer (producer, 2026-11-09): **Yes.** `budget.json` is per ContextHub host and ContextHub may run on several servers, so the proxy (the one shared component) owns the audit cap and live lease registry; ContextHub queries it. Follow-ups created: **LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK** (this worklog, child) and **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS** (ContextHub worklog).
- **Q: Which cross-host mechanism should AC1 use?** — Answer (producer confirmed, 2026-11-09): extend the proxy's reservation surface with an audit-tier lease (option a).
- **Q: When should the ContextHub item be created?** — Answer (producer, 2026-11-09): now. Created as `WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS` (top-level in the ContextHub worklog, `discovered-from:LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS`, blocked by the proxy child).
- **Plan-session revision note (2026-11-09, author: plan).** No new questions were asked during planning: the Appendix entries above (research + producer direction of 2026-11-09) already answer the mechanism choice (option a, proxy audit-tier lease), the budget-ownership move to the proxy, the repo mapping (control infrastructure vs audited targets) and the ContextHub-child timing. The decomposition follows those accepted answers verbatim; no prior answer was changed.

**Research summary:** The host-wide dispatch-budget ledger (`~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.json`, `maxAudit`) already serialises audits within one machine but is explicitly single-machine (`machine-coordination.ts`), and `budget.json` is read per host so multiple ContextHub servers can each believe they are under cap. The proxy already owns per-request admission tickets (`admission_reserve.py`) and sees all client hosts (`client_ip`, `X-Session-Id`), so producer direction moves audit-budget ownership there and has ContextHub query it. The audit skill's batch queue is physically host-wide (`XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-semaphores/audit-batch`) but entries carry no project identity, so cross-project routing and reporting are the gap. This yields a control-infrastructure change: proxy budget/admission (llm), audit-skill client/queue (SorraAgents), dispatcher query (ContextHub).

data.description:
# Right-size the llama-server prompt cache and checkpoint budget

**Headline:** The 40 GiB prompt cache saturates again — 39,829 of 40,960 MiB with
26 prompts on 2026-11-03, and 38.5 GiB resident right now — so this item
measures how much re-prefill is caused by eviction rather than by genuinely new
tokens, and right-sizes the two knobs that set per-prompt cost (`cache-ram` and
`ctx-checkpoints`) from that measurement rather than from the 16-prompt estimate
the current cap was derived from.

## Problem statement

When the prompt cache reaches its cap, llama-server evicts the oldest cached
prompt and that session's next turn becomes a full prefill of its whole context
(tens of thousands of tokens, up to several hundred seconds) instead of a short
delta prefill. The cache is currently sized from a per-prompt state estimate of
~2,013 MiB measured against a maximum of 16 concurrently-retained prompts; the
2026-11-03 incident shows 26 prompts with the cache at 97.2% of its cap and
592,452 prompt tokens consumed for 4,345 decoded tokens in 40 minutes. The
estimate and the real load have diverged, and nothing records whether the
resulting re-prefill is eviction waste or genuinely new work.

## Users

- **Proxy operator (agent, on-call, or the next maintainer)** — needs a cache
  budget that stops silently evicting under normal load, plus a recorded
  derivation and host-memory floor so the number is not re-litigated from a new
  round number.
- **Agent sessions on the local model** (pi sessions, herdr workers, remote LAN
  clients) — pay the re-prefill as minutes of first-byte latency on a turn they
  have effectively already sent.
- **Maintainers of the tuning docs and tests** — need the documented geometry,
  the pinning test and the configured values to agree, so drift is a red test
  rather than a future incident.

User stories:

- As an agent session returning to the local model after a pause, I want my
  prefix still resident so my next turn is a delta prefill, not a full one.
- As a proxy operator, I want the cache budget derived from a measured
  per-prompt size and a stated headroom floor, so a busy week cannot push the
  host into swap.
- As a maintainer, I want the cache numbers in `models.ini`, the tuning doc and
  the pinning test to agree, and the re-prefill attribution measured rather than
  assumed.

## Evidence

Recorded incident (2026-11-03, 08:30–09:10), from
`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` and `llama-server.log`:

| observation | value |
|---|---|
| prompt cache in use | 39,829 MiB of the 40,960 MiB cap |
| prompts retained | 26, several holding the full 32 checkpoints (2,925 / 2,998 / 2,494 MiB each) |
| cache update latency | 234 ms |
| slot `prompt_save` state written per task switch | 439 MiB |
| prompt tokens processed / decoded | 592,452 / 4,345 (≈136:1) |
| prefill rates in the log | median 122 tok/s; 143–303 tok/s for the large re-prefills; 598 tok/s best case |

Current live state (2026-11-18): host total 127,436 MiB, `MemAvailable`
46,907 MiB, 1,042 MiB of swap in use; the spawned Qwen3 child carries
`--cache-ram 40960`, `--swa-checkpoints 32`, `--parallel 2` and has been resident
since 2026-11-15 with RSS grown to 38.5 GiB — i.e. the cap is filling again
under normal load, three days after the last restart.

Prior measurements at the same cap, for contrast:

| window | cap | requests | evictions | max prompts held |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-12 (`docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-12.json`) | 32,768 MiB | 1,404 | 18 | 16 |
| 2026-10-18 (`docs/dev/prompt-cache-post-deploy-2026-10-18.json`) | 40,960 MiB | 380 | 0 | 11 |
| 2026-11-03 incident | 40,960 MiB | — | — | 26 |

The 2026-10-18 window recorded zero evictions, so the cap looked adequate then;
the growth to 26 retained prompts is a load change, not a regression in the
sizing arithmetic. That is precisely why the per-prompt constant must be
re-derived against the current prompt count instead of the 16-prompt figure.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Attribution is measured, not assumed** — over a fixed, named window a reproducible measurement (committed script or artifact) decomposes prefilled prompt tokens into (a) genuinely new tokens, where the prompt or prefix was never cached (new session or genuine divergence), and (b) re-prefills of a prefix that was previously cached and then lost, reporting the eviction-attributable share and token volume; the attribution method, its match rule and its error bounds or limitations are stated alongside the numbers.
2. **A trade-off table supports the recommendation** — the measurement produces a `cache-ram` x `ctx-checkpoints` trade-off table stating, per candidate configuration: prompts held, per-prompt state, the checkpoint term, killed prompts (prompts that would no longer fit), the checkpoint resume value (rollback granularity and the full-prefill risk of having fewer anchors), and MiB per prompt; the recommended pair is derived from that table and names the `MemAvailable` floor at which an increase must be refused.
3. **Applied, durable and pinned by test** — the chosen values are applied in `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` with a comment recording the measurement, its date and the derivation; the expectations in `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh` now assert the chosen values, and `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` states the same derivation so config, doc and test cannot drift apart.
4. **Post-change verification, deployed** — the change is deployed with `/skill:start-proxy --restart` (never by killing the proxy) and the spawned Qwen3 child is confirmed to carry the new flags; a post-change measurement over a window comparable to the AC1 baseline shows both the eviction-attributable re-prefill share and prefilled prompt tokens per request falling measurably, with the prompt-token-to-decoded-token ratio recorded alongside its workload caveat.
5. **No throughput or latency regression** — prompt-eval throughput and client-visible first-byte latency measured over the same before/after windows do not regress, or any movement is attributed with evidence to a named confounder rather than to this change.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

Local sessions stop losing their cached prefixes to eviction, so a returning session's first token arrives in seconds of delta prefill instead of minutes of full re-prefill.

## Constraints

- **Config must be durable**: values are set through `models.ini` `[Qwen3]`, not
  a one-off launch-script switch, so they survive a proxy restart (the precedent
  set by LP-0MUPPAC7R0053J8L AC7).
- **Host memory is shared**: 128 GiB unified memory, of which the model weights
  (24.6 GiB, `Q5_K_M`), the q8_0 KV cache and the prompt cache all draw from the
  same pool that the GPU uses. The documented invariant is
  `MemAvailable - cache-ram >= max(8 GiB, 10% MemTotal)` = 12,743.7 MiB.
- **The pinning test is a hard gate**: `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh`
  asserts `cache-ram = 40960` and `ctx-checkpoints = 32`; any change to either
  knob must update those assertions in the same commit.
- **llama-server logs carry no timestamps**: a measurement window is a *file
  set*, so the corpus (and its file list) must be recorded in the artifact's
  `meta` block for the before/after comparison to be reproducible.
- **Expected-but-not-an-error log line**: `forcing full prompt re-processing due
  to lack of cache data` is normal for this hybrid attention + recurrent
  architecture; the signal is its *volume* and the token count behind it, never
  the message itself.
- **Test execution routes through `/skill:test`**; no ad-hoc `pytest` runs.
- **Never kill the LLM proxy** — use `/skill:start-proxy --restart` for the
  deploy step.

## Existing state

- `models.ini` `[Qwen3]`: `cache-ram = 40960` (derived 2026-10-12 from
  2,013 MiB/prompt x 16 observed max x 1.25), `ctx-checkpoints = 32` (pinned at
  the llama.cpp default, with a comment explaining why it is not the lever),
  `swa-full` removed as a no-op for this arch.
- `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py` already measures requests, prompt tokens
  requested/reused/prefilled, full prefills split small/large, prefill wall time,
  eviction count and sizes, cache saturation and checkpoint overhead, and
  supports `--recommend`, `--json`, `--glob`, `--cache-ram-filter` and
  `--assume-cache-ram-mib`. It does **not** yet attribute a full prefill to an
  eviction, and `recommend()` proposes a `cache-ram` only — it reports the
  checkpoint term but does not vary it.
- Committed measurement artifacts: `docs/dev/prompt-cache-baseline-2026-10-01.json`,
  `-post-deploy-2026-10-07/10-12/10-15-partial/10-18*.json`.
- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` documents the sizing history, the checkpoint
  lever's "kept at 32" decision and the headroom invariant.
- The 2026-11-03 saturation is not yet measured with the tool: there is no
  artifact for that window, and no figure for how much of the 592,452 prompt
  tokens was eviction-caused.

## Desired change

Extend the measurement so a full prefill is attributed to an eviction rather
than to genuinely new work, then use that attribution to choose the
`cache-ram` / `ctx-checkpoints` pair, record the derivation in `models.ini` and
the tuning doc, pin it in the test, deploy, and verify the improvement on a
comparable window. The outcome is explicitly allowed to be "the current sizing
is correct and the residual re-prefill is genuinely new tokens" — provided the
measurement and the decision are recorded.

Three live items converge on one `models.ini` comment block and one
`ctx-checkpoints` value (`LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV`, `LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51`, this
item). Sequencing, not silent merging, is the mitigation — see the scope
boundaries and risks.

## Scope boundary and non-goals

- **Not** slot count or slot geometry (`LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8` territory; slot
  geometry was separately measured at 0 tok/s in
  `docs/dev/local-prefill-lever-comparison-2026-11-11.md`).
- **Not** KV-cache quantisation (`cache-type-k/v`) or weight quantisation.
- **Not** `force_full_prompt` / delta routing — that flag is load-bearing for
  this hybrid arch (LP-0MUPPAC7R0053J8L investigation) and removing it would
  break context, not improve caching.
- **Not** `ubatch-size` — measured and reverted (1.04x at ~27k tokens, below the
  1.3x gate); do not re-raise without a 40–80k-token measurement.
- **Not** the proxy's own disk slot save/restore path (`session_slot_*`), which
  is bypassed and worthless for a hybrid/recurrent model (llama.cpp#25913).
- **Scope boundary with `LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV`** ("Re-derive cache-ram with a
  MemAvailable floor", a blocked child of epic `LP-0MVZ9TQX4000DPTS`): that item
  owns the geometry sync test and the durable floor wording. This item's AC3
  writes the same comment block, so the two must not be implemented in parallel.
  If this item lands first it satisfies that slice's "measurement refresh", and
  the producer can close `LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV` as already covered rather than
  paying for a second derivation.
- **Scope boundary with `LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51`** ("Launch-flag A/B: threads and
  SWA checkpoints", blocked): that item has `--swa-checkpoints` (the
  `--ctx-checkpoints` alias) explicitly **in scope** as a benchmark A/B, and its
  own AC1 predicts the signal will be a change in the
  `forcing full prompt re-processing` path rather than raw throughput — i.e. the
  same question this item asks from production logs. The split is by method and
  evidence, not by knob: this item **consumes** any value that item has already
  measured and adopted (it becomes the candidate configuration), and **does not
  re-litigate** an adopted value silently — a conflict between the A/B result
  and this item's attribution measurement is recorded and escalated, not
  resolved by picking the friendlier number. Three items touching one knob is
  itself a sequencing risk worth flagging to the producer.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Attribution has no explicit join key.** The llama-server log does not tag a
  prefill with the cache entry it would have matched, so attribution must be
  inferred (for example: a full prefill whose token count matches a recently
  evicted entry within a bounded window, cross-checked against the proxy's
  per-dispatch `cached_ratio`). AC1 therefore requires the match rule *and* its
  error bounds to be stated, and a deliberately conservative classification is
  preferred over an optimistic one.
- **Raising `cache-ram` is not free.** The host is already at 46.9 GiB
  `MemAvailable` with swap in use; an increase sized against 26 prompts
  (~49 GiB by the current arithmetic) is unlikely to clear the floor. The
  checkpoint lever (halving `ctx-checkpoints` halves the ~2 GiB per-prompt term)
  is the likely answer, and it buys capacity at the cost of coarser rollback.
- **The headroom invariant double-counts a resident cache.** The documented
  check is `MemAvailable - cache-ram >= reserve`, which is a pre-allocation test;
  when the cache is already fully resident, only the *delta* is a real
  allocation. Whichever form is used must be stated in the recorded derivation,
  because the two give different verdicts today.
- **Fewer checkpoints can increase full prefills.** Fewer anchors means less
  chance of matching a reused prefix. If the checkpoint lever is taken, AC4's
  post-change measurement is what proves it helped rather than hurt, and the
  prompt-token-to-decoded-token ratio must not be the only evidence — it is
  workload-dependent and a quieter week would flatter it. Per-request metrics
  (`prefilled tokens/request`, `eviction-attributable prefills/request`) are the
  comparable ones.
- **Scope-creep risk**: the measurement will surface adjacent findings (cache
  update latency, `prompt_save` write volume, admission behaviour). These are
  recorded as observation bullets or as `discovered-from` work items, not
  absorbed into this item's ACs.
- **Assumption**: the 2026-11-03 window's logs are still available under
  `/var/log/llama-proxy/` (rotated or not) for the baseline; if they have
  rotated away, the baseline is the nearest surviving window and that
  substitution is recorded in the artifact with the corpus file list.

**Key Files:**

- `models.ini` — `[Qwen3]` `cache-ram` / `ctx-checkpoints` and the derivation comment block (AC2, AC3)
- `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py` — needs an eviction-attribution split in the summary (AC1) and a checkpoint term in `recommend()` (AC2)
- `tests/test_prompt_cache_analysis.py` — attribution and recommendation cases (AC1, AC2)
- `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh` — the two pinned assertions (`cache-ram = 40960` ~line 560, `ctx-checkpoints = 32` ~line 573) (AC3)
- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` — checkpoint-lever section, headroom invariant and the new measurement (AC3, AC6)
- `docs/dev/prompt-cache-<window>.json` — the committed before/after measurement artifacts (AC1, AC4)
- `proxy/proxy/` — read-only unless the proxy's per-dispatch `cached_ratio` is needed for the attribution cross-check (AC1)

## Related work

- **LP-0MUPPAC7R0053J8L** (completed) — the original prompt-cache right-sizing
  (8 GiB default -> 23,552 MiB), which built `scripts/prompt_cache_analysis.py`
  and `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` and first documented the checkpoint
  term as the dominant per-prompt cost.
- **LP-0MUYFC3C5004TCYN** and **LP-0MV5HSUHF002MDPG** (completed) — the
  32,768 MiB and 40,960 MiB cap raises, and the 2,013 MiB/prompt x 16 x 1.25
  derivation this item re-derives against 26 prompts.
- **LP-0MUPQIEK10079EAW** (completed) — the post-deploy verification pattern
  (baseline artifact, length-matched window, before/after table) that AC1 and
  AC4 should follow.
- **LP-0MVZ9TQX4000DPTS** (epic, plan_complete) — "Keep local prompt prefixes
  resident", whose AC3 is the cache-headroom commitment this item feeds; its
  child **LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV** is the overlapping derivation slice (scope
  boundary above) and **LP-0MW3GKXQS004F3CC** is the geometry sync test.
- **LP-0MVKU2J0T0023RRW** (blocked) — characterising restored-cache
  invalidation on this hybrid arch; relevant because it constrains what a
  checkpoint change can be expected to buy.
- **LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51** (blocked) — the launch-flag A/B on threads and SWA
  checkpoints. It has `--swa-checkpoints` in scope with the same re-prefill
  hypothesis, so its result is an input to AC2 rather than a separate answer
  (scope boundary above).
- **LP-0MWCEII0V003V76A / `docs/dev/local-prefill-lever-comparison-2026-11-11.md`**
  — the four-family prefill lever register (slot geometry 0 tok/s, quant at most
  1.9%, parallel prefill 1.00x), which is why cache capacity, not batch or
  geometry, is the lever left to pull here.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV** – Re-derive cache-ram with a MemAvailable floor (blocked)
- **LP-0MW3GKXQS004F3CC** – Cache geometry sync test (open)
- **LP-0MUPPAC7R0053J8L** – Right-size the llama-server prompt cache (--cache-ram) to stop 8 GiB saturation evictions (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance, already (+90 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, already, applied (+88 more)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance, already (+88 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**No producer questions were required for this intake.** The seed context
(2026-11-03 incident evidence plus three testable ACs) and the producer's
2026-11-05 answers on the parent epic resolved every open decision:

- Q: *May `cache-ram` be raised above 40,960 MiB, or must the fallback (reduce
  the checkpoint set / cap concurrent prompts) be the planned remediation?* —
  Answer (producer, 2026-11-05, recorded on `LP-0MVZ9TQX4000DPTS`): "Host RAM:
  128 GiB unified memory — cache-ram increase permitted subject to a stated
  MemAvailable floor." Source: `wl show LP-0MVZ9TQX4000DPTS` comment by Map,
  2026-11-05T11:14:47Z. Consequence: no producer gate on the cache-ram lever;
  the floor decides, which is why AC2 requires the floor to be named.
- Q: *Is reducing `ctx-checkpoints` acceptable given the documented "fewer
  checkpoints can increase full prefills" conclusion?* — Answer (research):
  acceptable only as the fallback, since AC2's original wording asks for "the
  measured trade-off stated" and AC3 explicitly permits a recorded no-change
  decision. Evidence: `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` comment block and
  `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` §"Checkpoint lever (AC3)". No question
  raised because the item already admits both outcomes.
- Q: *Does this item duplicate the epic's `LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV` ("Re-derive
  cache-ram with a MemAvailable floor")?* — Answer (research, duplicate-check
  procedure): partial overlap only. That item re-derives `cache-ram` and adds
  the MemAvailable floor plus a doc/test sync; it explicitly does not touch
  `ctx-checkpoints`, does not attribute re-prefill to eviction, and does not
  measure a post-change window. This item keeps those distinctive parts (AC1,
  AC2's checkpoint half, AC4) and records the shared-comment-block conflict as
  a scope boundary rather than rewriting the other item.

**Research summary.** The 8 GiB -> 23,552 -> 32,768 -> 40,960 MiB history, the
2,013 MiB/prompt derivation and the "checkpoint term is ~2 GiB of the ~2 GiB"
finding all come from `docs/dev/prompt-cache-tuning.md` and the
`docs/dev/prompt-cache-*.json` artifacts. The live confirmation (40,960 MiB
resident, RSS 38.5 GiB after 3.3 days, `MemAvailable` 46,907 MiB with swap in
use) was read from `ps`/`free` on 2026-11-18. The hard-pinned test assertions
were found at `tests/test_models_ini_centralized_config.sh:560-582`. The three
"prior measurement" rows were recomputed from the committed JSON artifacts.

## Plan (decomposition)

Decomposed into five child slices, created test-first and wired as a serial dependency chain (each slice is a vertical cut through code, tests, docs and — from slice 2 — a committed measurement artifact):

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs covered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Eviction-attribution fixtures and red tests (LP-0MWLZPTY1001QR4T) | task | — | AC1, AC2 (executable contract) |
| 2 | Attribute full prefills to evictions (LP-0MWLZPUKD000D2NG) | feature | 1 | AC1 |
| 3 | cache-ram x ctx-checkpoints trade-off table (LP-0MWLZPV7A005JZJD) | feature | 2 | AC2 |
| 4 | Apply and pin the chosen geometry (LP-0MWLZPVUG004ECFL) | feature | 3 | AC3, AC6 (code comments/doc) |
| 5 | Deploy and verify the post-change window (LP-0MWLZPWHO006NVVF) | task | 4 | AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7 |

Ordering rationale: the parent's outcome is explicitly allowed to be "the current sizing is correct", so the measurement (slice 2) and its table (slice 3) must produce evidence before any knob is touched (slice 4); the deploy and verification (slice 5) is a separate slice because it is the only one that interrupts service and because its evidence window is bounded by the restart.

Deploy sequencing recorded as an implementation note, not a plan dependency: `/skill:start-proxy --restart` kills llama-server, so any request in flight fails and the prompt cache restarts empty. The restart is detached and health-polled by the start-proxy skill, so it runs safely between tool calls; the post-change window starts at the restart timestamp.

Scope boundaries carried into the children (not merged silently): `LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV` (blocked) owns a slice of the same `models.ini` comment block and floor wording — slice 4 comments there recording that this item wrote the shared block; `LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51` (blocked) owns the `--swa-checkpoints` A/B — slice 3 consumes any value it has already adopted and escalates a conflict rather than picking the friendlier number.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-18: decomposed into 5 child slices (1 test, 3 feature, 1 verification) with a serial dependency chain; effort/risk re-estimated; plan Appendix recorded. No child closed, rewritten or duplicated (duplicate check found no fully-covered existing item; `LP-0MW3GKYAN009PQGV` is partial overlap and stays as a blocked sibling under the scope boundary above).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan session)

**No blocking producer questions.** The intake Appendix already records the producer's 2026-11-05 answers (cache-ram increase permitted subject to a stated `MemAvailable` floor; the checkpoint lever acceptable as the fallback), so the plan was resolved from repository evidence. Four research questions were answered from the tree and are recorded here for auditability.

- Q: *Does the 2026-11-03 incident window survive on disk for the AC1 baseline?* — Answer (research): No. `/var/log/llama-proxy/` retains daily rotation files from `llama-server.log-2026-11-04.gz` (922 B, effectively empty) onward; real content starts 2026-11-07. Consequence: the baseline is the nearest surviving saturated window, with the substitution and corpus file list in the artifact `meta` — the fallback the item's own risks section already allows. Evidence: `ls -l /var/log/llama-proxy/`, 2026-11-18.
- Q: *Which surviving window is the best baseline substitute?* — Answer (research): the surviving corpora are **busier** than the incident, so the substitution strengthens rather than weakens the evidence. Cache-state maxima measured 2026-11-18: 26 prompts (2026-11-07), 27 (11-08), 24 (11-09), 29 (11-10), 31 (11-11 and `llama-server.2.log`, 14 MB), 11 (11-12), 47 (11-13). Candidate baseline named in slice 2: 2026-11-13 (largest prompt count).
- Q: *Which `cache-ram` x `ctx-checkpoints` candidates belong in the AC2 table?* — Answer (research): `ctx-checkpoints` in {32, 16, 8} x `cache-ram` in {current 40,960 MiB, the measured requirement at the observed prompt maximum, the same capacity reached with a halved checkpoint term}, plus any value already adopted by `LP-0MVNBJY2R004EZ51`. Rationale: the checkpoint term is ~2 GiB of the ~2 GiB per-prompt cost, so halving checkpoints halves per-prompt state; the item's risks section names this as the likely answer while requiring the reported resume-value cost. No producer decision needed — both levers are already authorised by the intake Appendix.
- Q: *Is it safe to run the AC4 deploy inside an agent session?* — Answer (research, plan assumption): Yes, as its own slice. `start-proxy.sh --restart` is detached by default and health-polled, and it runs between tool calls; the restart kills llama-server, so an in-flight request from any concurrent session fails and the prompt cache restarts empty. The deploy slice records the restart timestamp as the start of the post-change window. OPEN QUESTION (producer awareness, **non-blocking** — the plan does not depend on the answer): if the producer prefers the restart to be operator-executed during a quiet window, slice 5 still applies unchanged — only who runs the command changes.

## Goal

Decide deliberately whether the second local slot is capacity or waste, and make the system use it (or stop advertising it as available).

## Evidence (incident 2026-11-03)

- llama-server runs 2 slots (total_slots=2, n_ctx 131072 each) and session_slot_pool_size is 2, but from task 191941 (08:43) through roughly task 193700 every launch was slot id 0 -- about 1,200 consecutive tasks on one slot. Slot 1 reappeared at task 193715 only once two requests genuinely overlapped.
- Normal agent traffic is not slot-pinned: id_slot is set only by compaction_summarizer.py; mainline requests let llama-server choose, and it picks by prompt-prefix similarity (1,040 selected slot by LCP similarity versus 39 by LRU). With the proxy granting one dispatch lease at a time there is never a second in-flight request, so slot 0 always wins and slot 1 is never launched.
- The signals disagree: available_slots reported 0 (lease-derived) at 08:50:47 while llama had a free slot, and 2 at 08:49:31 while the lease gate denied a dispatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Root cause recorded with supporting log evidence for why slot 1 goes unused in serialised operation, including the LCP-similarity versus LRU selection behaviour.
- AC2: A decision is recorded: either (a) enable deliberate two-session concurrency with cache-aware placement (so a second session is routed to a slot whose prefix it can reuse, avoiding a second full prefill), or (b) treat the local model as a single-slot resource for admission purposes and stop counting the idle slot as capacity in status and in client capacity decisions.
- AC3: The chosen option is implemented behind tests: a two-concurrent-session test asserts either two slots are used with reused prefixes, or the second request waits with an accurate capacity signal.
- AC4: Docs (models.ini slot commentary and docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md) are updated to match the decision.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MW1VVKPF001ZAV5** – Bound the slot snapshot with local_slots_max_snapshot_age_seconds (completed)
- **LP-0MRO4U5O1008TLFU** – Write multi-slot tests for poll_slots_for_model() (completed)
- **LP-0MSHFGO0M003Q5BL** – Fix /llama/local/status slot counts (missing model param) and expose per-slot details (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, accurate (+117 more)
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+117 more)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+117 more)

## Goal

**As an** operator, **I want** a measured verdict on the two chain/routing fixes shipped on 2026-11-03, **so that** "it is fixed" is a claim backed by a like-for-like before/after comparison against the configuration's own scheduled windows — not by the absence of complaints.

**Earliest implementation time: 2026-11-04 04:00 UTC.** That is the end of the first remote-closed window (`01:00-04:00` UTC) that completes after the 2026-11-03 14:25:10 UTC restart, so it is the first instant with (a) ≥13.5 h of post-fix log and (b) a full scheduled-gap sample. See **Timing** for why 2026-11-04 10:00 UTC is the *preferred* like-for-like point.

discovered-from:LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK, discovered-from:LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5.

## What is deployed

| Item | Commit | What it should change |
|---|---|---|
| LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK — fail fast on a provably dead chain | `7892d22d` | no chain hold when every provider is deterministically skipped or terminally refused; earliest-reset `Retry-After`; a `remote-ok` request is never bounced onto a chain with no capacity |
| LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5 — diagnosable lease occupancy | `763ed61f` | `local_dispatch_denied` carries the full occupancy evidence; `local_occupancy_divergence` names contradictions; stale records cannot block |

Deployed by restart **2026-11-03 14:25:09–14:25:10 UTC** (proxy pid 158427; `llama-server` and TTS relaunched and all three healthy). **The post-fix measurement window starts at 2026-11-03 14:25:10 UTC** (log rotation line `14:25:10,847 - INFO - Rotated previous proxy log`). Anything before that line is pre-fix.

## Timing: when the fix can actually fire

`model=code` has 7 providers; the gates that create a *provably dead* chain are the `available_times` windows:

| Provider | `available_times` (UTC) | Closed |
|---|---|---|
| `local-qwen3` | unrestricted | — |
| `munitoai-free` | unrestricted | gated only by usage-limit reset / quota |
| `opencode-go`, `opencode-go-2`, `opencode-go-3` | `00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00` | **01:00–04:00**, **06:00–10:00** |
| `deepseek-flash` | `00:00-01:00, 04:00-06:00, 10:00-00:00` | **01:00–04:00**, **06:00–10:00** |
| `munitoai` | `10:00-23:00` | **23:00–10:00** |

So the chain is *window*-dead only in **01:00–04:00** and **06:00–10:00** UTC, and it is only *provably* dead when `munitoai-free` is also out (usage-limit reset / quota) — which is exactly the 2026-11-03 08:41 shape. `munitoai-free`'s recorded reset was `2026-11-04T00:02Z`, so **the 01:00–04:00 gap on 2026-11-04 may legitimately have a live provider and therefore no trigger**; that is correct behaviour, not evidence of anything.

Therefore:

- **earliest defensible evaluation:** 2026-11-04 **04:00 UTC** (first complete post-fix gap);
- **preferred like-for-like evaluation:** 2026-11-04 **10:00 UTC**, i.e. the end of the `06:00–10:00` gap — the same clock window as the baseline below;
- if neither gap produced a trigger, conclude **inconclusive** (say so explicitly) and re-check at the next gap or at the next usage-limit/quota block rather than recording a fake pass.

## Baseline (pre-fix)

Recorded evidence, for the record:

- 2026-11-03 **08:41:42** — every remote provider deterministically skipped (`munitoai-free` `usage_limit_reset_pending` reset ~15.4 h away; `opencode-go-3` `quota_exhausted` ~14 days; four entries `outside_available_window`) and the proxy logged `Chain exhausted ... holding 300s before restarting cycle` **three times**. The audit subprocess (`audit-RISE-0MVZEOVQG0075XSU-...`) received a 429 in 0.4 s and could never succeed; its 1080 s per-call screen budget was consumed by holds.
- 2026-11-03 **08:40:05** — `Returning first provider error response instead of generic exhausted message ... (status=400)` followed immediately by two 300 s holds (the first provider's raw 400 carried no `Retry-After`, which is what re-enabled the "legacy full hold").
- 2026-11-03 **08:49:40** — local guard refused with `eta_prefill_s=45.2 enforced=true` and the request was routed onto the dead remote chain (`outcome=exhausted`); **08:50:41** the identical prompt and identical ETA were admitted (`enforced=false`, `eta_occupancy_s=0.0`) and produced a first byte in 6 s.
- 2026-11-03 **08:49:31.690** — `local_dispatch_denied session=... owner=... active=1` on a two-slot pool while `/llama/local/status` at 08:49:31.034 reported `available_slots=2`: the refusal named an owner and a count but not which gate refused.

### Measured baseline — log file `proxy.log.2026-11-03_101625`, window 08:37:26 → 10:16:25 UTC (99 min)

This is the pre-fix window captured by the log rotated at the 10:16 restart. It sits inside the `06:00–10:00` closed gap, i.e. it is the like-for-like comparison window.

| Signal | Count (99 min) |
|---|---|
| `Chain exhausted for model=` (holds taken) | **105** — 36 of them `holding 300s`, plus 30 s / 120 s / 38 s / 17 s variants |
| `All providers exhausted for model=` | 189 |
| deterministic-skip vocabulary | `usage_limit_reset_pending` 1198 · `outside its available_times window` 884 · `quota_exhausted` 1230 |
| `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` | 137 |
| … of which `reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` | **57** (11 distinct sessions) |
| `local_dispatch_denied` | 26 (none carrying occupancy evidence) |

### Control window — open windows, no trigger expected

`proxy.log`, 10:16:29 → 13:34:50 UTC (3 h 18 m; remote windows **open** that whole time): `Chain exhausted` **0**, `All providers exhausted` **0**, `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback` 334 (46 × `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` — correct fall-throughs, because remote had capacity), `local_dispatch_denied` 97. Use this as the "no trigger + open chain" reference: it shows what a *healthy* zero looks like, and it is why "0 holds" alone proves nothing.

Log retention is 7 days (`Pruned old rotated log ... > 7 days old`), so the baseline file survives until ~2026-11-10. Re-extract the numbers above if it is needed after that; do not assume it is still there.

## Measurement technique

Rules that keep the comparison honest:

1. **Like-for-like windows only.** Compare post-fix samples taken inside a *closed* window (`01:00–04:00` / `06:00–10:00` UTC) against the baseline above. Never compare an open-window sample against it; an open chain cannot trigger the fix, so it will always look "fixed".
2. **Normalise per hour** — sample lengths will differ; report counts per hour as well as raw counts.
3. **Check chain aliveness before interpreting a zero.** If no trigger fired, prove the chain was actually provably dead in that window (`munitoai-free` unavailable *and* the four window-gated providers closed). A zero with a live chain is `inconclusive`, not `fixed`.
4. **Exclude the restart verification probe** from the sample: session `verify-lp-0mw0kzr7a003ufqk-restart` (2026-11-03 14:25:54, 18/8/26 tokens) exists only to prove the deploy.
5. **Quote the log line, not the count**, for anything that decides the verdict — a count can be satisfied by a wrong reason.

### LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK (fail fast / no bounce) — expected post-fix signatures

```bash
LOG=/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log            # or the rotated file covering the chosen window
# 1. the fail-fast line replaces the hold, on one vocabulary
grep -c 'chain_planned_unavailable'          $LOG    # expect > 0 in a provably-dead window
grep -m3 'chain_planned_unavailable'         $LOG    # inspect reason=, hold=skipped, retry_after=, deterministic_skips=, terminal=
# 2. no hold on a provably dead chain
grep -c 'Chain exhausted for model='         $LOG    # expect 0 in that window (baseline: 105/99 min)
# 3. the local override instead of a bounce onto a dead chain
grep -c 'local_admission_guard_local_wait'   $LOG    # expect > 0 where the old code emitted direct_fallback
grep 'local_admission_guard_direct_fallback' $LOG | grep -c 'reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct'   # expect 0 *while the chain is dead* (baseline 57)
# 4. retry timing is honest (earliest reset, body == header, capped)
grep 'chain_planned_unavailable' $LOG | grep -o 'retry_after=[0-9]*' | sort -u
# 5. the client-visible shape (the preserved first error, now timed)
grep 'Returning first provider error response' $LOG | tail -3
# 6. the report renders the new section
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24   # "## Chain-end outcomes"
```

Targets:

| Metric | Baseline | Target |
|---|---|---|
| `Chain exhausted` (holds) per closed-window hour | 105 / 1.65 h ≈ **64/h** | **0** where every skip is deterministic; unchanged for transient chains (cooldown / 5xx / connection error) — verify at least one transient hold still occurs |
| `chain_planned_unavailable ... hold=skipped` | 0 (line did not exist) | > 0, one per affected request (not per provider) |
| `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` with a dead chain | 57 / 99 min | **0**, replaced by `local_admission_guard_local_wait` |
| `All providers exhausted` reached from a local ETA refusal | the 08:49:40 shape | **0** |
| audit-* call latency on a doomed chain | 300 s × 3 holds before the error | < 1 s |
| Advertised `retry_after` | cap-derived (3600) or absent | the earliest known reset, capped by `max_retry_after_seconds`, equal to the `Retry-After` header |

Per-line acceptance (AC2/AC4 of the item):
- `local_admission_guard_local_wait` must appear **with** `reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct` and **without** a following `→ routing to next provider` line;
- `chain_planned_unavailable` must **not** appear in a window where a provider was merely cooling down (that would be a false positive — the verdict must stay conservative).

### LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5 (diagnostics) — this half is measurable within hours

Denials happen under local contention (26 in 99 min pre-fix; 97 in 3 h 18 m), so this verdict does not need a closed window:

```bash
LOG=/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log
# every denial must carry the evidence suffix (fields: records_total, records_active,
# records_unexpired, records_stale, active_counter, max_local, generating,
# prefill_in_flight, prefill_cap, llama_available_slots, llama_total_slots, records=…)
grep -c 'local_dispatch_denied'                                  $LOG
grep -c 'local_dispatch_denied.*records_total='                  $LOG    # expect == the count above
# contradictions are logged, and the "our own numbers cannot explain it" class must be zero
grep -c 'local_occupancy_divergence reason=llama_reports_free_slots'  $LOG   # > 0 is fine (prefill cap vs llama view)
grep -c 'local_occupancy_divergence reason=occupancy_unexplained'     $LOG   # must be 0 — non-zero is a bookkeeping defect, file it
# which cap refused is now readable without a repro
grep -m3 'local_dispatch_denied' $LOG | grep -o 'generating=[0-9]*\|prefill_in_flight=[0-9]*\|prefill_cap=[0-9]*\|max_local=[0-9]*'
```

Targets: 100 % of `local_dispatch_denied` lines carry the evidence; `occupancy_unexplained` **0**; the 08:49:31 question ("denied with `available_slots=2` — which gate?") answerable from the line alone (expect `prefill_in_flight=1 prefill_cap=1`, i.e. the serialised-prefill cap, for that shape).

## Decision criteria

| Outcome | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **fixed** | a provably-dead window shows ≥1 `chain_planned_unavailable ... hold=skipped`, **0** holds, and the evidence suffix on every denial | close with the numbers; no follow-up |
| **partial** | fail-fast fires but a hold still occurs on a deterministic chain, or a denial lacks the evidence suffix | file a `test-failure`/bug item naming the exact line and reason; do not close |
| **not fixed** | a provably-dead window still shows `Chain exhausted` / `direct_fallback`, and no `chain_planned_unavailable` | reopen LP-0MW0KZR7A003UFQK (or file a new bug) with the window and the log lines |
| **inconclusive** | no provably-dead window occurred in the sample | record it, keep the item open, re-check at the next gap/usage-limit block; never record a pass |
| **regression** | holds disappear on *transient* chains too (cooldown/5xx), or `occupancy_unexplained` > 0 | treat as a defect: the verdict is over-firing |

If any outcome requires code change, create the follow-up item (`discovered-from:<this id>`) and implement it in its own worktree — this item is measurement only.

## Out of scope

- Changing provider `available_times` or adding an always-on remote provider (the operator rejected that on 2026-10-31; see LP-0MVWC9CZH004OZYN).
- Extending the classifier or the `chain_planned_unavailable` vocabulary — that is now owned by epic LP-0MVWC9CZH004OZYN (its AC11, extend-never-fork).
- Re-litigating the incident's per-call budget arithmetic.

## Candidate follow-up observed during the restart (not measured here)

Before the 2026-11-03 14:25 restart, `/llama/local/status` reported `llama_server_running=true`, `available_slots=2/2`, `capacity_hint=idle` for ~3 hours while **no `llama-server` process existed** (`llama-server.log` ends `start-llama.sh: line 273: 4168 Killed` at 11:33) and local dispatches were failing with `ConnectError`. `/health` said `healthy` throughout. That is a stale *running-state* divergence (distinct from the slot-count divergence fixed in LP-0MW0KZTWC004HXQ5): file it separately with this evidence if it reproduces — it is a candidate for the same "engine view vs route view" family.

## Assumptions

- The deployed code is what runs: proxy started 14:25:09 UTC, `dev` HEAD `7892d22d` committed 12:54 — confirm again at evaluation time with `ps -o lstart= -p <pid>` and `git log -1 --format=%cI dev`.
- `munitoai-free` remains the only unrestricted remote, so every provably-dead window is of the shape above; if a provider is added or re-timed, re-derive the window table before comparing.
- The 7-day log retention is long enough to reach the earliest evaluation date; if it is not, the baseline numbers in this description are the record.

## Scheduling hold (do NOT implement before the gate instant)

The title carries the earliest instant, but a title cannot stop `wl next` from
dispatching this item tonight, which would produce a premature sample. The item
is therefore parked with a **descriptive timer hold** as its assignee:
`not-before-2026-11-04T04:00Z` (a non-empty assignee is a scheduling hold, so
`wl next` skips it). This is a timer label, not an agent claim — no agent owns
this item.

At or after **2026-11-04 04:00 UTC**, release it and implement:

```bash
wl update LP-0MW0S88WJ005SBPH --assignee "" --json    # release the timer hold
wl show LP-0MW0S88WJ005SBPH --json                    # then /skill:implement <id>
```

If you are reading this *before* the gate instant because someone released the
hold early, do not measure: say so, re-apply the hold, and wait for the first
complete closed window. If the 01:00–04:00 gap on 2026-11-04 turns out to have a
live `munitoai-free`, the preferred sample is the 06:00–10:00 gap, evaluated at
2026-11-04 10:00 UTC.

## Goal

**As an** operator reading the after-acceptance eviction signal, **I want** a local dispatch that **completed successfully** to be released without being reported as `local_eviction_after_acceptance`, **so that** the AC7(a) defect detector (LP-0MVN4LCQJ0034S5S) counts real evictions instead of ordinary lease expiry.

## Evidence (2026-11-03 14:25:54 → 14:26:34 UTC, `dev` `7892d22d`)

A small verification request that **succeeded in 0.57 s** was 40 s later reported as an eviction after acceptance:

```
14:25:54  routing_check provider=local-qwen3 ... estimated_tokens=8
14:25:54  [local] POST ...  Stream finished: reason=length tokens=18/8/26 stream=false
14:25:54  lease_renewed session=verify-... timeout=30s
14:25:54  local_preference_resolved preference=remote-ok outcome=local reason=none
14:26:34  local_eviction     ... reason=slot_assignment_freed slot=0
14:26:34  local_eviction_after_acceptance ... reason=idle_timeout estimated_tokens=8
          new_tokens=8 eta_prefill_s=0.0 elapsed_s=40.1
14:26:34  lease_released session=verify-... reason=idle_timeout
```

Three things are wrong together:

1. `local_eviction_after_acceptance` is documented as "accepted local dispatches evicted **before their first byte**" — this request produced its first byte (and its last) within 0.57 s, so it was never evicted *after acceptance* in the intended sense;
2. `elapsed_s=40.1` is the *lease's* idle lifetime (30 s timeout + slack), not the request duration — so the field mixes two different clocks;
3. the event is emitted on the routine `lease_released ... reason=idle_timeout` path, which is the normal way every completed local dispatch's record expires.

Measured frequency in this window: 7 `local_eviction` lines, 6 `reason=slot_assignment_freed` (expected churn) and 1 `reason=idle_timeout` — i.e. 100 % of the `idle_timeout` eviction reports in the sample are false positives, and the true-positive rate of the signal cannot be established while that is the case.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The `local_eviction_after_acceptance` event is emitted only when a dispatch was admitted and did **not** reach its first byte (the documented meaning); a completed or cancelled-after-first-byte dispatch releases silently or under its own reason.
- AC2: `elapsed_s` measures the request's own lifetime (admission → release), not the lease timeout, so the value agrees with the request's observed duration.
- AC3: A regression test drives the pattern above — one local dispatch that completes, then the idle lease release — and asserts **no** `local_eviction_after_acceptance` line; a second test drives a genuine admitted-then-never-first-byte dispatch and asserts the line **is** emitted with a truthful `elapsed_s`.
- AC4: Existing consumers keep working: `local_eviction_after_acceptance` stays a distinct event from `local_eviction`, its `reason` vocabulary is unchanged, and the usage-analysis report's after-acceptance breakdown (which splits by reason) still renders.
- AC5: Documentation of the event's meaning in `proxy/docs/routing.md` matches the behaviour.

## Out of scope

- The eviction reasons themselves (`measured_cache_deficit`, `prefill_deadline`, `idle_timeout`) and their thresholds.
- Any change to how leases are released — only to what is *reported* about the release.

## Key files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` — the `local_eviction` / `local_eviction_after_acceptance` emitters.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — the idle-timeout / slot-assignment-free release paths and the dispatcher that records the event.
- `proxy/tests/` — `test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py`, `test_lease_truthfulness.py`, and the usage-analysis `test_post_acceptance_eviction_report.py` contract.

## Assumptions

- The `slot_assignment_freed` line emitted immediately before it is the expected churn line and is not part of the defect.
- The window's single occurrence is representative of the routine path (every completed local dispatch leaves a record that later expires by `idle_timeout`), not a one-off; AC1/AC3 make that checkable rather than assumed.

## Provenance

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MWKQJHSM000CI6W** – [bug] local_eviction_after_acceptance reports the umbrella reason no_progress_watchdog for pre-deadline early aborts, so the AC3 reason-rate criterion can be met by relabelling (open)
- **LP-0MSIC2UJX007C0IR** – Implement adaptive lease for anonymous sessions (completed)
- **LP-0MVO7IDTP005S92D** – Session-eviction slot_assignment_freed evictions are false positives and leak per-endpoint leases (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — matched: 0mw0kzr7a003ufqk, 0mw0kztwc004hxq5, 30s, abandoned, ac1 (+178 more)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — matched: 0mw0kzr7a003ufqk, abandoned, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+174 more)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — matched: 0mw0kztwc004hxq5, abandoned, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+173 more)
